name: CoreWeave
description: CoreWeave rents out AI computing: it builds and runs data centres full of GPUs with its own orchestration software and leases the capacity, mainly under multi-year take-or-pay contracts, to AI labs and large technology companies. It operated 43 data centres with over 850 MW of active power at the end of 2025 and about 3.1 GW contracted. The contracts are big and lumpy: Microsoft was about 67 percent of 2025 revenue, and remaining contracted revenue (RPO) rose from $15.1 billion to $60.7 billion during 2025 and $103.7 billion by June 30, 2026. It is barely profitable at the operating line (a $46 million operating loss in 2025) and pays $1.2 billion of net interest a year because it funds data centres mostly with asset-level debt secured by those customer contracts.

employees.note: 1,967 in the US and 222 in 19 other countries (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: CoreWeave Cloud Platform
businessLines.how: Customers sign multi-year committed contracts to buy a fixed amount of GPU capacity on a take-or-pay basis with a pay-as-you-go on-demand option also offered; CoreWeave borrows against each contract to buy the GPUs and build the data centre.
businessLines.description: Infrastructure services (GPU compute), managed software services, and application software services including storage, Mission Control, SUNK (Slurm on Kubernetes) and Weights & Biases developer tools.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 operating income $324M; H1 2026 operating loss $(193)M vs $(8)M

whatsNext.text: Delivery of 393 MW at one site and 355 MW at other sites, expected in phases between 2026 and 2028
